name: Interior design and fit-out

problems.words: Clients keep changing the design after we've started
quick_ideas: Get a written sign-off at the end of each design stage, so changes after it are clearly changes
Tell clients up front how many revisions are included.

workzap_build.text: A project file with drawings, revision history and client sign-off at every stage, so each change is counted and visible.

problems.ask_first: How many revisions does a client usually get?
problems.free_stops: Stage gates and sign-off flow are in the solution document.

problems.words: Change orders are agreed on WhatsApp and then disputed
quick_ideas: Confirm every change in one written message with its cost before work starts
Keep a running list of agreed changes per project.

workzap_build.text: A change-order flow where the client approves cost on WhatsApp and the item goes straight onto the bill.

problems.ask_first: Who works out the extra cost when a change comes in?
problems.free_stops: The approval and billing steps are in the solution document; disputes go to a lawyer.

problems.words: Our quotes are wrong because the site measurement was off
quick_ideas: Use the same measurement checklist on every site visit
Ask for photos with dimensions, so the office can double-check.

workzap_build.text: A site measurement form on phone with photos and dimensions feeding the quote directly.

problems.free_stops: Form fields and the link to pricing are in the solution document.

problems.words: We win jobs at a price that leaves no margin, and can't say if we made money
quick_ideas: Take one finished project and compare quoted against actual material and labour
Note which items ran over most.

workzap_build.text: A quote builder with a rate library that shows margin before sending, and a project P&L of quoted against actual for every job.

problems.ask_first: How do you build a quote today?
problems.free_stops: Rate library structure and margin rules are in the solution document.

problems.words: Imported tiles and lighting take months and hold up the site
quick_ideas: List long-lead items per project with order date and need-on-site date
Order those first, as soon as the design is signed.

workzap_build.text: A procurement tracker showing supplier, lead time and expected delivery against site need date for every item.

problems.ask_first: Which materials take longest to arrive?
problems.free_stops: Tracking stages and alerts are in the solution document.

problems.words: Trades step on each other — painter comes before the electrician finishes
quick_ideas: Write the trade sequence for each site on one page
Confirm the previous trade is finished before booking the next.

workzap_build.text: A trade schedule per site in the right sequence, sending each trade its day plan on WhatsApp.

problems.ask_first: Which trades are in-house and which are subcontracted?
problems.free_stops: Sequencing rules per project type are in the solution document.

problems.words: Joinery workshop is overloaded while site waits
quick_ideas: Put this week's workshop jobs in order of site need date
Share that list with project managers.

workzap_build.text: A workshop job board with stages and completion dates per project.

problems.ask_first: How do you plan what the workshop makes each week?
problems.free_stops: Workshop stages and planning logic are in the solution document.

problems.words: Clients complain they don't know what's happening on site
quick_ideas: Pick one fixed day a week to send each client a short update with photos
Name one contact person per client.

workzap_build.text: Weekly progress photos and status sent to each client automatically.

problems.ask_first: How do clients get updates now?
problems.free_stops: Update content and timing are in the solution document.

problems.words: Snag lists drag on and the client holds back the last payment
quick_ideas: Walk the site with the client and agree one final snag list
Close each item with a photo.

workzap_build.text: Snag and warranty tickets with photos and sign-off, alongside milestone billing with reminders.

problems.ask_first: Which milestone payment is hardest to collect?
problems.free_stops: Snag flow and billing triggers are in the solution document.

problems.words: Leads come from Instagram but most just want free ideas
quick_ideas: Ask a few qualifying questions before any meeting, so serious clients surface
Be clear that design work starts after a design fee.

workzap_build.text: Lead intake from Instagram and website with qualifying questions and source tracking.

problems.ask_first: Where do most enquiries come from?
problems.free_stops: Question set and scoring are in the solution document.

never_say: Any advice on removing walls, load-bearing changes, ceiling loads, gas moves, rewiring or fire-rated materials; a qualified engineer or licensed trade decides.
Any help skipping mall or authority approvals or using non-compliant materials.
Any view on contract disputes, withheld payments or liability for defects; that is for a lawyer.
Any request to record clients' names, home addresses or contact details.
Any help copying another studio's designs or using images without permission.

sample_reply.person: Is there a way to stop clients changing their minds mid-project and expecting the same price? We redid one kitchen three times.
sample_reply.pi: Yes, this can be brought under control, and you can start this week. 1) Get a written sign-off at the end of each design stage, so any later change is clearly a change. 2) Confirm every change in one written message with its cost before work begins. Workzap can do this automatically for you: stage sign-offs, change orders the client approves on WhatsApp, and each one added straight to the bill. Shall I prepare a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
